updates.description: New versions download quietly in the background. You decide when to restart.

ai.title: AI & Claude
ai.description: Godmode drives the Claude Code CLI as the brain of every agent. These defaults apply unless an agent overrides them.
ai.bypassOffToastDescription: Agents will pause at permission prompts — unattended automations may stall.

model.title: Model
model.description: Agents can pick their own model; this is the default.
model.defaultDescription: Opus 5.5 is tuned for long, autonomous multi-step work.
model.fallbackDescription: Used automatically when the default model is overloaded.
model.effortDescription: Higher effort thinks longer before acting — better results, more tokens.
model.ultracodeUnsupported: {{model}} doesn't support dynamic workflows — pick a model that does.
model.ultracodeMissing: The installed Claude Code doesn't offer dynamic workflows.

autonomy.title: Autonomy
autonomy.description: How much your agents may do without asking.
autonomy.onBody: They can run any shell command, install software, and create, edit or delete files on this machine — exactly like a coworker with full access. This is what lets automations finish unattended. Vault secrets stay protected: in fill mode the AI never sees your passwords, and every secret use is audited.
autonomy.offBody: Every command or file edit needs approval. Nobody is watching an automation, so unattended work will stall until you turn full bypass back on.

limits.title: Limits
limits.parallelDescription: How many agent runs may execute at the same time. Extra runs wait in a queue.
limits.timeoutDescription: A run is stopped after this long.
limits.compactDescription: Once a chat fills this much of the model's memory, it is summarized by itself and goes on from the summary. Earlier keeps every step faster and cheaper; later keeps more detail. Compress by hand any time with the ring next to the model, or /compress.
limits.autoContinueDescription: When Claude's usage limit stops a run, it waits and continues by itself once the limit has reset — where it stopped.
limits.resumeDescription: Chats, automations and handed-over tasks that were working when Godmode quit, updated or crashed pick up where they stopped once it is back (work of the last day). Turns that broke off because Claude couldn't be reached continue once the internet is back, and a turn that ended while its background work still ran picks that up. Board tickets always do.
limits.watchdogDescription: Stops runs that stall or go in circles, with a report of where they stood. Board tickets try again once on their own.
limits.stalledDescription: No sign of life for this long. A tool that is still running gets three times as long, at least 30 minutes.
limits.loopDescription: The same tool with the same input and result, this many times in a row.

every.title: Every agent

every.label: Instructions for every agent
every.example:
1. Commit as me only — never add an AI co-author.
2. Keep code comments to a minimum.
3. Merge main into your branch and fix conflicts before opening a pull request.
4. For UI changes, attach screenshots of the new feature.

stays.title: What stays with you
stays.body: A connected app works as Godmode, your built-in agent, and inside its limits. It never sees a password or a 2FA code, only which logins exist, and it can't open settings, backups or files. It does see what agents were asked and what they answered. Agents it creates may use saved logins but not read them, and can't manage other agents or control this computer until you allow it. Every change is in the audit log under Security.

created.tryPrompt: Create a Godmode agent that checks our competitors' pricing every Monday morning and sends me a summary.
created.tryTitle: Try it in a new Claude Code session
created.asks: Claude Code asks before it uses a Godmode tool for the first time. {{command}} shows the server and its tools.
created.installError: Godmode couldn't add itself to Claude Code
created.runHint: It adds Godmode to Claude Code for every project. Then start a new session.
created.configHint: For apps set up with a JSON file (Cursor, Claude Desktop, Windsurf…). The app starts the connection itself, and it finds Godmode on whichever port it runs.
created.claudeHint: Adds Godmode to Claude Code for every project.
created.urlHint: For apps that take an address and a header. It stops matching if Godmode ever starts on another port; the config file doesn't mind.
created.cliHint: tools lists what the key can do, call runs one tool with JSON arguments. Handy for scripts.
created.footerManage: It can set up and steer your team. Remove it anytime in the list.
created.footerRead: It can look, and change nothing. Remove it anytime in the list.

devices.title: Devices
devices.description: Use Godmode on several Macs as one. Chats can run on any of them and move between them, also while they work.
devices.port: The other computers reach this one on port {{port}}. If they can't connect, allow it in your firewall.

alone.title: One Godmode, on every Mac.
alone.body: Every Mac has your agents, logins and chats, and chats can move between them, also while they work. One is the primary — keep it on (a Mac mini or a desktop); while it's away, another Mac stands in.
alone.addDescription: Make this Mac the primary and invite another one.
alone.joinDescription: Make the invite on the Mac that should be the primary: Settings → Devices → Add a computer.
alone.whereBody: Every computer keeps a copy of the agents, logins, settings, the task board, automations and your to-dos, and changes travel both ways. The primary runs the schedules. Each chat lives on the computer it runs on, and every computer of the group sees all of them.

invite.label: Invite
invite.step1: On the other Mac, open Godmode
invite.step1Body: Settings → Devices → Join with an invite.
invite.step2Body: It works once and only for a few minutes. Joining takes about ten seconds.
invite.step3PrimaryBody: Keep it on. The other Mac takes its agents, logins and settings; its own chats stay and show up here too.
invite.step3Body: It takes the group's agents, logins and settings. Its own chats stay and show up on every computer of the group.

join.toastDescription: Its agents, logins and settings are here now.
join.runnerCode: That's a runner's pairing code. Here, paste an invite from another Mac; it starts with {{prefix}}
join.notInvite: That isn't an invite. It starts with {{prefix}} — copy all of it, line breaks don't matter.
join.expired: This invite has expired. Make a new one on the other Mac.
join.takesSetupBody: Its agents, logins and settings replace the ones here. The chats on {{computer}} stay, and show up on every computer of the group.
join.connecting: Connecting to {{name}} and copying its setup…

group.computersDescription_one: {{count}} computer in this group. Chats can run on any of them.
group.computersDescription_other: {{count}} computers in this group. Chats can run on any of them.
group.noOthers: No other computer yet. Add one to share this Mac's Godmode.
group.invitePrimary: Paste this invite in Godmode on the other Mac.
group.inviteSecondary: The invite comes from {{name}}: the new computer joins the group there.

status.bodyStanding: {{name}} is away, so {{computer}} runs the automations, the task board and the phone app until it's back. Everything that changes here goes back to it then.
status.bodySecondary: {{name}} runs the schedules. {{computer}} has a copy of everything and keeps working while it's away. Chats can run here or on any other computer of the group.
status.bodyPrimarySolo: It runs the schedules for the group. Keep it on and awake.
status.bodyPrimaryAll: It runs the schedules for all {{count}} computers. Keep it on and awake.
status.bodyPrimaryAllStandIn: It runs the schedules for all {{count}} computers. Keep it on and awake — while it's away, another computer stands in.

standInNow.activeSince: Since {{time}} the automations, the task board, messaging and the phone app run here.
standInNow.active: The automations, the task board, messaging and the phone app run here.
standInNow.pending_one: {{count}} change goes back when {{name}} is back.
standInNow.pending_other: {{count}} changes go back when {{name}} is back.
standInNow.pendingNone: What changes here goes back when {{name}} is back.
standInNow.takesOverIn: {{computer}} takes over in {{time}}. Everything keeps working.
standInNow.takesOverSoon: {{computer}} takes over in a moment. Everything keeps working.
standInNow.otherStandsIn: {{name}} stands in for it. Everything keeps working here too.
standInNow.waitsHere: Everything keeps working here. Automations, messaging and the phone app wait until it's back.

standIn.title: While the primary is away
standIn.description: Every computer has a copy of everything, so nothing stops when the primary sleeps or its lid closes. With Tailscale on each computer they also find each other on different networks, so only one of them does the work.
standIn.label: Another computer stands in
standIn.on: When {{subject}} is away for {{minutes}} min, another computer runs the automations, the task board, messaging and the phone app until it's back.
standIn.onElsewhere: When {{subject}} is away for {{minutes}} min, another computer runs the automations, the task board, messaging and the phone app until it's back. Change this on {{name}}.
standIn.off: Automations, messaging and the phone app wait until {{subject}} is back.
standIn.offElsewhere: Automations, messaging and the phone app wait until {{subject}} is back. Change this on {{name}}.

signIns.ownLine: With your saved logins, 2FA codes and passkeys.
signIns.seedLine: A computer new to a site copies the primary's sign-in.
signIns.title: Browser sign-ins
signIns.description: How the other computers get signed in to websites.
signIns.label: Sign-ins on each computer
signIns.own: Each computer signs in by itself with your saved logins, 2FA codes and passkeys. Copying a sign-in can sign you out of Google and others.
signIns.ownElsewhere: Each computer signs in by itself with your saved logins, 2FA codes and passkeys. Copying a sign-in can sign you out of Google and others. Change this on {{name}}.
signIns.seedSelf: A computer that isn't signed in to a site yet starts with {{computer}}'s sign-in. Google and others may sign you out when they see it twice.
signIns.seedElsewhere: A computer that isn't signed in to a site yet starts with {{name}}'s sign-in. Google and others may sign you out when they see it twice. Change this on {{name}}.

handoff.title: Closing the lid?
handoff.body: Hand the running work to {{to}}. Chats stop here and continue there with everything they did so far. Open the lid later and it's all here.
handoff.idle: Nothing is working on {{computer}} right now.
handoff.label: Hand off to

fda.title: Needs Full Disk Access
fda.self: Agents here stop at a macOS “allow access to Desktop?” question until you click Allow.
fda.other: Agents on {{name}} stop at a macOS “allow access to Desktop?” question until someone clicks Allow there.
fda.dialogDescription: Then agents there can open the Desktop, Documents and Downloads without macOS asking first. Do this on {{name}}:
fda.step1Body: Apple menu → System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access.
fda.step2Body: Not in the list? Click + and pick Godmode from Applications. macOS asks for the Mac's password.
fda.step3Body: The warning here goes away by itself.

twin.uninstalled: {{chats}} The runner is switched off there.
twin.stillStarts: {{chats}} Its runner still starts there: run “{{command}}” on {{there}} to switch it off.
twin.error: Couldn't switch off the runner on {{there}}
twin.title: Also paired as a runner
twin.body: {{name}} also runs as a runner from an earlier setup.
twin.confirmBody: The old runner on {{there}} is switched off and removed. {{moves}} The app keeps working as it does now.
twin.moves_one: Its chat moves to the app there, with everything it did so far.
twin.moves_other: Its {{count}} chats move to the app there, with everything they did so far.
twin.movesNone: Its chats move to the app there.

row.confirmBody: It works on its own again, with the setup it has now. The chats that live on it stay there and no longer show up on the other computers.
row.confirmBodyWorking_one: It works on its own again, with the setup it has now. The chats that live on it stay there and no longer show up on the other computers. {{count}} chat is working there right now.
row.confirmBodyWorking_other: It works on its own again, with the setup it has now. The chats that live on it stay there and no longer show up on the other computers. {{count}} chats are working there right now.

older.title: Older runners
older.description: Paired as runners before device groups. Their chats keep working here, but new chats don't start there.
older.removedDescription: Its chats stay here, as chats of {{computer}}.
older.forget: Godmode forgets this runner, and the runner forgets {{computer}}.
older.chats_one: Its chat stays here with everything in it; new messages in it are answered on {{computer}}.
older.chats_other: Its {{count}} chats stay here with everything in them; new messages in them are answered on {{computer}}.
older.working_one: An agent is still working there — what it finishes from now on won't show up here.
older.working_other: {{count}} agents are still working there — what they finish from now on won't show up here.

runOn.title: Chats
runOn.description: Where new chats work. Each chat can still move to another computer, also while it works.
runOn.label: New chats run on
runOn.single: Other computers show up here while they're online.
runOn.multi: You can pick another computer for each chat as you start it.
runOn.failover: Continue work when a computer goes away
runOn.failoverOn: When a computer's lid closes while it works, {{target}} takes the work over after a few minutes. Handing off first keeps the agent's whole session.
runOn.failoverOff: Work stops while its computer sleeps and goes on when it's back.

leave.labelPrimary: Every computer works on its own again
leave.descPrimary: The other computers leave and keep the setup they have now. Chats that live on them stay there.
leave.descSecondary: It stops sharing with {{name}} and keeps a copy of the setup it has now, and its own chats.
leave.confirmDissolve_one: The other computer leaves and works on its own again, with the setup it has now. Chats that live on it stay there and no longer show up here.
leave.confirmDissolve_other: All {{count}} other computers leave and work on their own again, with the setup they have now. Chats that live on them stay there and no longer show up here.
leave.confirmLeave: {{computer}} stops sharing with {{name}} and works on its own again, with a copy of the setup it has now. Its own chats stay here; chats on {{name}} stay there.

importMemory.description: Another assistant already knows a lot about you. Copy it over once, and your main agent knows you from day one.
importMemory.ask: Ask {{name}} to write out what it remembers
importMemory.askOther: Ask the assistant to write out what it remembers
importMemory.tooLong: That is more than {{max}} characters — paste the most important part.
importMemory.hint: Your main agent keeps what matters, merges it with what it knows and leaves out passwords and keys.

license.title: License
license.description: Your Godmode Pro licence: every feature, on this computer.

activate.title: Activate Godmode
activate.description: Every feature in every plan. Your agents, chats and logins stay on this computer.
activate.remote: Add the licence key in Godmode on the computer itself.

license.changeDescription: The new key is checked before it replaces the one ending in {{hint}}.
license.removeEnforced: Godmode stops starting new work on this computer until a key is added again. Your subscription itself isn't changed.
license.removeFree: Your subscription itself isn't changed; you can add the key again any time.
license.notEnforced: This is a build of your own, so it doesn't need a licence: Godmode is open source under the MIT License. Godmode Pro is for the official apps from usegodmode.com.

logs.copiedDescription: Paste it into a chat with Claude · {{size}}
logs.title: Logs
logs.description: A private record of errors, slow spots and how runs went. Copy it into a chat with Claude to track down bugs and make Godmode faster.
logs.fixInCodeHint: An agent gets this log as a ticket, fixes the causes in Godmode's code and merges the fix
logs.masked: Passwords, 2FA codes, API keys and tokens are masked before anything is written. Nothing leaves this device unless you copy it.

verbose.title: Detailed logging
verbose.description: For chasing a specific problem. Turn it off again afterwards — the log fills much faster.
verbose.label: Record every request and tool call
verbose.labelDescription: Adds the timing of every API request and agent tool call, plus debug details from all parts of Godmode.

confirm.title: Delete the diagnostic log?
confirm.bodyCount_one: All {{entries}} entry is removed, including the desktop app's own log. Godmode keeps recording from now on — handy after you've shared the log and the problems are fixed.
confirm.bodyCount_other: All {{entries}} entries are removed, including the desktop app's own log. Godmode keeps recording from now on — handy after you've shared the log and the problems are fixed.
confirm.body: All entries are removed, including the desktop app's own log. Godmode keeps recording from now on — handy after you've shared the log and the problems are fixed.

repair.title: Self-repair
repair.description: “Fix in code” files a ticket on Godmode's source repository. Agents with the self_repair tool check the logs by themselves, too.
repair.repoDescription: Godmode's source code, or your fork of it. Godmode pushes and merges with this computer's git and GitHub sign-in.
repair.branchDescription: Fixes start from it and are merged into it.
repair.agentDescription: Works on the fixes. They go on its workspace's board.
repair.mergeDescription: A delivered fix is merged into {{branch}} right away, without a review.

issues.title: Needs attention
issues.description: Warnings and errors that keep coming back, grouped by what they say.
issues.none: Nothing needs attention — no warnings or errors recorded.

list.description: Newest first. Click an entry for its details.
list.emptyDescription: Errors, slow spots and finished runs will show up here as Godmode works.
list.limit_one: Showing the newest {{count}}. Search or filter to find older entries — Copy and Download include everything.
list.limit_other: Showing the newest {{count}}. Search or filter to find older entries — Copy and Download include everything.

memory.title: Memory
memory.description: Agents remember your preferences, facts and learnings across conversations — stored in each agent's own git repository on this machine.

backend.title: Memory backend
backend.filesDescription: Each agent keeps <c>MEMORY.md</c> and a <c>memory/</c> folder. Plain text you can read and edit — nothing to install.
backend.claudeMemDescription: Automatic, searchable long-term memory via the open-source claude-mem plugin. Captures context from every session; data stays inside the agent's repo.

import.title: Bring your memory
import.label: Import from another AI
import.description: What ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini remember about you — your work, people, preferences and plans — goes into your main agent's memory, so it knows you from day one.

housekeeping.title: Housekeeping
housekeeping.injectDescription: The agent starts each new chat already knowing its <c>MEMORY.md</c> — no need to look things up first.
housekeeping.autoCommitDescription: Snapshots the agent's memory, transcripts and files into git so you can see — and undo — what changed.
housekeeping.reflectDescription: The agent spends a moment writing down what it learned (costs a few extra tokens, makes it noticeably smarter over time).

dreaming.title: Dreaming
dreaming.description: While you're away, agents review their recent conversations and rewrite their memory: they pick up what they learned, merge duplicates, fix contradictions and update dates — like sleeping on it — keep it short enough to load into every chat, and sort their workspace. Every dream can be reviewed and undone in the agent's Memory tab.
dreaming.enabledDescription: Agents consolidate their memory in the background, on the schedule below.
dreaming.scheduleDescription: In this computer's local time. Dreams missed while it was off or asleep are caught up when it wakes.
dreaming.expectedFields_one: Expected 5 fields (minute hour day month weekday), got {{count}}
dreaming.expectedFields_other: Expected 5 fields (minute hour day month weekday), got {{count}}
dreaming.modelDescription: What stays in memory, what moves into a note and what goes is a judgment every later chat lives with — Opus is the default. A smaller model dreams for less.
dreaming.sizeDescription: Dreams keep <c>MEMORY.md</c> under this and move the details into notes in <c>memory/</c>. Every chat starts with it, so shorter means cheaper, quicker chats. A chat loads up to {{limit}} characters — an agent whose memory outgrows that dreams as soon as it is idle, without waiting for the schedule.
dreaming.tidyDescription: Dreams also sort <c>workspace/</c>: loose files into topic folders, leftovers of finished work out. Recent files and anything an automation uses stay put; what goes waits a week in <c>workspace/tmp</c>, and undoing the dream puts it all back.
dreaming.offers: Offer to take work off your plate
dreaming.offersDescription: Your main agent's dreams also spot work it could do for you — a chore you repeat, a deadline nobody is on, a task left half-done — and offer it on Home. Nothing starts until you click Do it.
dreaming.minExchangesDescription: A scheduled dream waits until the agent has had at least this many new exchanges since its last one.
dreaming.refreshDescription: Without enough new activity, still dream when the last dream is this old and the memory mentions dates — so plans that have passed become past events. 0 = never.

claudeMem.installedDescription: Agents use it from their next run.
claudeMem.ready: claude-mem {{version}} is installed. Each agent keeps its own isolated store.
claudeMem.missing: claude-mem isn't installed yet — until it is, agents keep using <c>MEMORY.md</c>.

pairPhone.title: Connect your phone
pairPhone.description: Scan the code with the Godmode app. It works once and only for a few minutes.
pairPhone.connectedBody: Chats, agents and live screens are on your phone now. You can remove it anytime in this list.
pairPhone.qrLabel: Pairing code for the Godmode app
pairPhone.step1Gateway: Get Tailscale, or use Godmode Cloud
pairPhone.step1GatewayBody: With Tailscale signed in to the same account as this computer, your phone reaches Godmode directly. Without it, the phone goes through Godmode Cloud, which this computer is linked to.
pairPhone.step1GatewayBodyTailnet: With Tailscale signed in to the same account as this computer ({{tailnet}}), your phone reaches Godmode directly. Without it, the phone goes through Godmode Cloud, which this computer is linked to.
pairPhone.step1Body: Sign in with the same account as this computer. Your phone reaches Godmode through it, never over the internet.
pairPhone.step1BodyTailnet: Sign in with the same account as this computer ({{tailnet}}). Your phone reaches Godmode through it, never over the internet.
pairPhone.step2Body: Tap Scan QR code, or point your camera app at the code.
pairPhone.step3Body: The phone gets its own key. This code can't be used again.

phone.title: Phone
phone.description: Control Godmode from your iPhone or Android phone: chats, agents, automations and the screens they work on. Phones connect over Tailscale, or through Godmode Cloud when this computer is linked to it. No port is opened to the internet.
phone.remoteOnly: Pairing phones and changing phone access only work in Godmode on the computer itself.
phone.accessGateway: Paired phones may connect, over this computer's Tailscale address or through Godmode Cloud. Godmode only answers phones you paired.
phone.accessTailscale: Paired phones may connect. Godmode listens only on this computer's Tailscale address, and only answers phones you paired.
phone.portDescription: Change it only if another app uses it. Paired phones need a new code afterwards.

paired.title: Paired phones
paired.description: Each phone has its own key. Removing a phone disconnects it right away.
paired.unavailable: The list of phones isn't available here.
paired.empty: No phones yet. Connect one to use Godmode on the go.

can.title: What a phone can do
can.body: Chat with agents, stop runs, run automations, start and stop VMs, and watch browsers, shared screens and VMs live. It can only take control of browsers and of screens you shared in a chat. Logins, 2FA codes, backups, integrations and settings can't be opened from a phone.

hero.title: Your coworkers, in your pocket.
hero.body: Hand over a task from anywhere, follow the answer as it's written, and look over an agent's shoulder in its browser or VM.
hero.needs: Needs Tailscale on this computer and your phone, or a link to Godmode Cloud.

device.confirmDescription: It's disconnected right away and can't control Godmode anymore. You can pair it again with a new code.

security.rememberOnDescription: The vault key is stored in your OS keychain.
security.rememberOffDescription: You'll enter your passphrase after every restart.
security.title: Security
security.description: Your vault, how agents may use secrets, and who can reach the dashboard. Every secret access is audited.

vault.title: Vault
vault.description: AES-256-GCM encrypted. The key is derived from your passphrase and only lives in memory — or in your OS keychain if you allow it.
vault.lockDescription: Agents can't use logins or 2FA codes until you unlock again.
vault.passphraseDescription: Change the passphrase that protects your vault.
vault.rememberDescription: Stores the vault key in the macOS Keychain / Windows Credential Manager so automations can run unattended after a restart. Turn off for maximum security on shared machines.
vault.autoLockDescription: Lock the vault after this many idle minutes. 0 = never.

secrets.title: Agents & secrets
secrets.description: Defaults for new agents. Each agent can be adjusted individually.
secrets.fillDescription: Godmode types passwords and 2FA codes straight into the page. The AI never sees them.
secrets.revealDescription: The AI may read raw passwords and codes — needed for API-only tools. Every reveal is audited.
secrets.redactDescription: Mask every known password, token and code in transcripts, run logs and the live stream.
secrets.iconsDescription: Show login icons from Google's favicon service. This tells Google which sites you have saved; turn off for maximum privacy.

web.title: Web dashboard
web.description: Use Godmode from any browser with `godmode serve`. Host, port and remote access apply after a restart.
web.passwordNotSet: Not set — only the access token (`godmode token`) can sign in.
web.remoteDescription: Listen on your network instead of only this computer (127.0.0.1).
web.exposeTitle: Only expose Godmode through a reverse proxy with TLS
web.exposeBody: Anyone who reaches this port can try to sign in to a coworker with full access to your machine and vault. Put it behind HTTPS (e.g. Caddy, Cloudflare Tunnel or Tailscale), set a strong dashboard password, and restrict allowed origins.
web.noPassword: No dashboard password is set yet.
web.hostLocal: Loopback only while remote access is off.
web.originsDescription: Extra origins allowed to call the API (one per line), e.g. the HTTPS URL of your reverse proxy.

remoteConfirm.title: Allow remote access?
remoteConfirm.description: Godmode will accept connections from other devices after a restart. Only do this behind a reverse proxy with TLS, and set a strong dashboard password first.

system.title: System
system.description: Health of the tools Godmode relies on, and where your data lives.

check.title: System check
check.description: Everything agents need to work. Missing pieces can be installed with one click.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.description: What Godmode may do on this computer: its own files, its tools, and what the system lets it see and control.

updates.title: Updates
updates.description: The tools Godmode has installed, and their versions.
updates.nothingInstalled: The update finished without installing anything.
updates.none: No tools are installed yet — install them from the system check above.

upkeep.title: Automatic upkeep
upkeep.description: Let Godmode look after its tools in the background.
upkeep.autoUpdateDescription: Godmode looks for new versions a few times a day and installs them while no agent is working.
upkeep.autoFixDescription: Repairs the permissions of Godmode's own files and installs required tools again when they went missing. It never opens a system dialog on its own.

install.title: Installation
install.help: Something off? Open the logs to copy them for Claude, or run {{command}} in a terminal.

setup.title: Setup
setup.label: Run onboarding again
setup.description: Walk through the setup wizard again. Your data, vault and agents are kept.
setup.confirmDescription: You'll see the welcome wizard again. Nothing is deleted — steps that are already done (like the vault) are skipped.

vms.grantReason: Enter your vault passphrase to let agents type your logins and 2FA codes into their VMs.
vms.title: Virtual machines
vms.summary: Give agents their own macOS: they install tools, run builds and use apps in an isolated VM on this Mac instead of on your computer. A run uses its chat's VM, else its agent's, else its workspace's.
vms.offNote: Every run works on this Mac while it's off, and VM controls leave chats and agent settings. Your VMs stay as they are.
vms.pointOwn: A macOS of their own for each agent or chat
vms.pointIsolated: Installs and builds stay off your computer
vms.unsupported: Virtual machines aren't available on this machine
vms.unsupportedReason: macOS VMs need a Mac with Apple silicon.
vms.isolate: Keep agents with a VM off this Mac
vms.isolateDescription: Claude Code's own Bash tool — which runs on this Mac — is turned off for their runs and permissions aren't bypassed, so commands can't touch your computer and file tools only reach the agent's repository, the chat's folder and the VM's shared folder.
vms.idleDescription: Frees memory and CPU when no run used a VM for this long. 0 = keep them running.

fill.title: Logins and 2FA codes
fill.description: Let agents sign in to websites and apps inside their VM with the logins and 2FA codes from your vault.
fill.label: Type logins and 2FA codes into VMs
fill.labelDescription: In the VM's Chrome, logins are filled like on your Mac — only on the login's own website. In other apps, Godmode types into the field the agent clicked. Either way the value never passes through the AI, but the agent controls the VM, so a determined agent could capture what's filled there. Turning this on asks for your vault passphrase.
fill.factTyped: Typed by Godmode, not the AI
fill.factApps: In apps, not bound to a website

quit.title: When Godmode quits
quit.description: What happens to running VMs. Their disks are always kept.
quit.suspendDescription: Their memory is saved to disk — they resume where they left off.
quit.stopDescription: macOS shuts down in each VM; the next start boots fresh.
quit.keepDescription: They stay up; Godmode picks them up again when it starts.

tart.description: Runs the VMs with Apple's Virtualization framework — <link>tart.run</link>, free for personal use.
tart.notInstalled: Not installed — Godmode installs Tart {{version}} when you set up or create a VM
tart.image: Downloaded image — new VMs from it are ready in seconds. Removing it frees the space; existing VMs keep working.
tart.imageWithSize: Downloaded image · {{size}} GB — new VMs from it are ready in seconds. Removing it frees the space; existing VMs keep working.
tart.customDescription: Leave empty to use Godmode's own copy (installed on demand) or one on your PATH.

voice.sample: Hi, I'm Godmode — your AI coworker. I'll take care of the busywork so you can focus on what matters.
voice.noSynthesis: Speech synthesis is not available in this browser
voice.title: Voice
voice.description: Talk to your agents and hear their answers — hands-free, like a call with a coworker.

mode.title: Voice mode
mode.enableDescription: Shows the microphone in chat and enables spoken replies.
mode.autoSpeakDescription: When you dictate a message, the answer is read aloud automatically.
mode.languageDescription: BCP-47 code used for speech recognition and synthesis.

stt.title: Speech to text
stt.browserDescription: Free, uses your system's speech recognition.
stt.openaiDescription: OpenAI Whisper-class transcription — more accurate, needs an OpenAI API key.

tts.title: Text to speech
tts.description: Browser voices are free; OpenAI and ElevenLabs sound more natural.
tts.elevenlabsVoiceDescription: Copy it from the voice library at elevenlabs.io.

openai.description: Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works (e.g. a local server).

keys.title: API keys live in the vault
keys.body: Add your {{providers}} key under <link>Integrations → API keys</link>. Keys are encrypted and never shown again.
